sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Stoddard County?
sections.html:
Two offices in Bloomfield split the work. The Assessor lists and values property, and the Collector of Revenue sends the bills and takes the money. Both sit on South Prairie Street in the county's government building.

  • Collector of Revenue: 401 S. Prairie St, P.O. Box 80, Bloomfield, MO 63825; (573) 568-3327; open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, closed on state and federal holidays.
  • Assessor: 401 South Prairie, P.O. Box 307, Bloomfield, MO 63825; (573) 568-3163. Its site has real estate and personal property searches by account, name or address.

Stoddard County sits in the southeast corner of Missouri. It covers 823 square miles of land, the seat is Bloomfield and the largest city is Dexter, with Advance, Bell City, Bernie, Dudley, Essex and Puxico also incorporated, according to the county's Wikipedia entry. Part of Mingo National Wildlife Refuge lies inside its borders.

sections.h2: When are Stoddard County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The Collector starts accepting payment on November 1, and the bill is due by December 31. Statements go out by mail in November, once the Clerk's tax books reach the Collector in the fall.

Late charges are added on the first of each month after the deadline, and the amounts are printed on your statement. A mailed payment has to carry an official U.S. Postal Service postmark by the end of the month, because the office will not accept a payment that is short of the penalties added. According to its FAQ, missing a bill does not cancel the penalty either.

Ways to pay include cash in the office, personal check, money order, cashier's check and credit card online or by phone (with a convenience fee). A drop box near the entrance of the government building takes payments at any hour, but a late payment left there without the penalty is returned. The office's resources page warns that anything paid through a mortgage escrow account does not show in the online database.

sections.h2: Can I pay Stoddard County property tax in installments?
sections.html:
Yes, for real estate tax, through a monthly program in place since the 2010 tax year. Payments are based on what you paid last year, divided by eleven: ten equal installments, then a final one for the balance that is actually due. The Collector's installment page says money comes out of a checking or savings account on automatic withdrawal, on the 5th or the 20th as you choose.

  • Delinquent real estate tax makes you ineligible. Prior year taxes must be paid first.
  • Parcels with mortgage escrow cannot enroll.
  • If a payment fails, the plan may be ended, and penalties on any tax unpaid by December 31 remain yours.

sections.h2: Is there a senior tax freeze in Stoddard County?
sections.html:
There is a credit that locks the homestead bill. Starting in 2024, an eligible resident aged 62 or older on January 1 who owns and lives in the home can freeze the real estate tax on it. The Senior Citizen Tax Credit page states plainly that it is not an exemption, since you still pay the bill.

New applicants apply from January 1 through June 30. Renewal forms are mailed from February 1 and are due by June 30. The first application must be notarized, and your driver's license or state ID has to show the address. Homestead means the primary residence and up to five acres, so barns and commercial or agricultural ground fall outside it.

The page also covers new construction and additions, so ask the Collector at (573) 568-3327 how a sale or a remodel affects the frozen base year before you list.

sections.h2: How do I dispute an assessment in Stoddard County?
sections.html:
Contact the Assessor first at (573) 568-3163, and ask for the county's Board of Equalization filing deadline. At the board, RSMo 138.060 says no presumption favors the assessor's value, and in a county like this one the assessor carries the burden of proof for a property whose assessed value rose at least 15% since the previous assessment, unless new construction or improvement caused the rise.

If you pay while contesting, RSMo 139.031 requires full payment before the delinquency date and a written statement of the grounds filed with the Collector. A lawsuit for recovery then has to start in circuit court within 90 days of the protest.

sections.h2: What happens to delinquent taxes and a Stoddard County sale?
sections.html:
Delinquent land can be sold on the fourth Monday in August under RSMo 140.150. The Collector has to mail the first notice to the record owner by first class mail. A second notice by certified mail is required when the assessed valuation is above $1,000. The Collector's site lists delinquent tax certificate sales.

For a seller, the practical rule comes from the Collector's FAQ: taxes follow the property, not the person. The statement goes to the buyer, and you and the buyer decide at closing who pays. A buyer is expected to check the tax status before purchase, so expect the title company to ask for a payoff or a proration. Missouri's Property Tax Credit claim, Form MO-PTC, is a state refund for some seniors, disabled owners and renters, and the Department of Revenue explains eligibility.

sections.h2: What does the local economy mean for sellers in Stoddard County?
sections.html:
The county's job base is modest. QuickFacts counts 644 employer establishments in 2023 with total employment of 8,455 and an annual payroll of about $389 million. Retail sales were $572,476,000 in 2022, or $20,165 per resident.

About 56.7% of people aged 16 and over are in the civilian labor force, and the mean commute is 23.1 minutes. Of adults 25 and older, 83.7% finished high school and 16.7% hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Median selected owner costs are $1,110 a month with a mortgage and $443 without one. For the current levy on a parcel, read the rate lines on the tax statement or ask the Collector, because the posted levy page is an archive of rates by township that runs through 2022.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Stoddard County homes?
sections.html:
Homes here are priced far below the $276,800 median for St. Louis County. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table lists a median owner-occupied value of $143,300 for 2020 to 2024, against 71.8% owner-occupancy.

School districts that reach into the county include Advance R-IV, Bell City R-II, Bernie R-XIII, Bloomfield R-XIV, Dexter R-XI, Puxico R-VIII and Richland R-I. Density is 34.8 people per square mile, and the 2020 census found 66.4% of residents living in rural areas.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Stoddard County property tax?
faqs.a: At the Collector of Revenue, 401 S. Prairie St in Bloomfield, or by mail to P.O. Box 80, Bloomfield, MO 63825. Online payment is also offered through the Collector's website.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Stoddard County taxes?
faqs.a: December 31. The Collector begins accepting payment on November 1, and extra charges are added on the first of each month after the deadline.

faqs.q: Does the county offer a payment plan?
faqs.a: Yes, for real estate tax. It uses ten equal monthly withdrawals and an eleventh payment for the remaining balance, and it cannot be used for delinquent taxes or escrowed parcels.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax when I sell my house?
faqs.a: You and the buyer decide that at closing. The Collector says the statement should be forwarded to the buyer and that taxes follow the property.

faqs.q: How old do I have to be for the senior freeze?
faqs.a: You must be 62 or older as of January 1, own the home and live in it as your primary residence. New applicants file between January 1 and June 30.
